parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal entry and document rules are operative (passport sex-marker restrictions in effect after Nov 2025; refusal for document discrepancy; fraud-ground lifetime-ineligibility risk). Federal immigration custody and federal corrections policy document forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse and conversion-style treatment. The division adds a documented 2026 episode: victims were charged rather than attackers, one was denied hospital care, and she was jailed in a men's facility and searched by a male guard despite her marker. A severe municipal restroom ordinance and a 2023 minors' care ban also apply. Mitigations are limited: national hate-crime law, a 2015 marriage ruling, and state employment recourse that is largely absent. The trans-specific killing rate is an undercount floor and is not used. Custody by birth sex with documented harm is the worst operative feature.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports show sex at birth; new X markers not issued. Cable refuses cases with document discrepancy and raises a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility. Passports confiscated or blocked, leaving some stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; litigation pending, with the Supreme Court having allowed restrictions to take effect.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal can move into fraud allegation and detention, and the regime is enforced by allied-government advisories.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse of trans men. Division jail: trans woman held in men's facility, searched by male guard despite female licence marker; denied hospital care.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Driver's licence marker does not govern housing or search; document match provides no custody protection.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal rules bar gender-identity-congruent facilities in government-funded settings. Four states criminalise restroom use in some circumstances; one arrest documented with handcuffing and 24h men's-ward holding. Municipal restroom ordinance described as among the most severe. No statewide facilities statute described for this state.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No statewide facilities statute documented; two municipalities protect in employment, housing and accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Municipal ordinance and jail placement combine; federal policy reaches all government-funded facilities.

care_services.exposure: Minors' gender-affirming care banned since 2024; state excludes transition care from insurance and low-income coverage; federal proposals to bar public reimbursement for under-18s; victim denied hospital care in 2026.
care_services.interaction: Denial of care to an injured trans person combined with custody placement raises emergency-care exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as targets for neutralisation. Executive orders direct prosecution of teachers for social transition support. Division police charged victims of a mob attack.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism powers said not to target mere disagreement; 2009 national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing of trans advocacy as a security concern raises exposure for visitors who are engaged with advocacy.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minors' care banned; federal subpoenas of hospital records for under-19s; school-facing prosecution directives. A travelling minor's marker and care needs may trigger scrutiny at entry and in custody.
minors_guardians.protection: Court injunctions have blocked several orders; outcome unresolved.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's guardian presenting documents that differ from the minor's presentation may face entry refusal and a fraud allegation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Mob beating of a trans couple over restroom use (Aug 2026), with police charging victims and no attacker arrested. A 2024 prison killing is recorded. Trans-specific killing rate is an undercount floor and is not used.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; state hate-crime law omits gender identity; no state anti-discrimination law for gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims were charged rather than attackers, so the police response reverses recourse; denial of hospital care followed.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Oversight findings recur without changing practice. Statewide restroom position not established. Outcome of the victims' charges unresolved. Passport litigation unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National courts have blocked several orders; federal employment discrimination ruling; two municipal protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are mostly national or municipal and do not operate reliably at state or custody level.

anchor_checks.comparison: Anchor 0.35-A has a universal entry register and exclusion with no effective remedy. This dossier has similar entry refusal for document discrepancy and fraud exposure, but no statewide exclusion register is documented and custody harm is documented, so it sits slightly lower.

Anchor 0.25-C has birth-sex housing and a cross-dressing arrest statute with documented assaults. This case shares birth-sex custody and documented assault, with a comparable restroom arrest. It is similar in tier, with the added federal entry and fraud exposure pushing it slightly lower.

Anchor 0.45-D has universal registration and nightly database transmission. This dossier lacks documented universal registration, but it has documented custody harm and state-tolerated charging of victims, so it sits lower.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets a layered regime: federal document refusal and fraud exposure at entry, federal immigration custody with documented sexual abuse and forced labour, and a state/division custody practice that places a trans woman by birth sex and denies hospital care. A mob attack in which victims were charged rather than attackers shows state response reversing recourse. Restroom criminalisation exists in some states, and this state's statewide facilities position is not established. Mitigating national hate-crime law and court injunctions are partial and do not operate reliably in custody. The trans-specific killing rate is discounted as an undercount floor. The worst documented feature is birth-sex custody with harm, a tier-one exposure, placing the case in the high-risk band.
